newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Decision near on big Sogo Australia plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Decision near on big Sogo Australia plan.

text.p: A decision is imminent on a Japanese-led proposal to replace Sydney's biggest hole in the ground with one of the city's biggest new buildings.

Joint-owners of a central-city site derelict since 1987, Japanese construction giant Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd and leading retailer Sogo Co Ltd, are behind a development application now awaiting approval by the Sydney City Council's Central Sydney Planning Committee.
The application has been lodged by builder Multiplex Constructions (NSW) Pty Ltd, which will handle construction.
An official with the council's city development division confirmed that the application had been lodged and said a decision was expected at the committee's next meeting, in a couple of weeks.
The planned development encompasses a 41-storey office tower which would rise above an entry lobby, an arcade of speciality shops and three department store floors.
Sogo will share the retail area with speciality shops, a consultant with Sogo's Sydney representative, Caburah Holdings Pty Ltd, told Reuters. The final split is yet to be determined.
"After many years, it's getting to the stage where something is about to happen," he said. "We believe it's going ahead."
The final matter to be settled involves car parking.
The development application incorporates a carpark for 300 cars while council planners prefer a smaller version for 162 cars, Caburah's spokesman said.
"We would expect (this) to be resolved in discussion with council over the next few weeks. I trust it's not something that would ultimately stop the process going ahead," he said.
Present plans under a signed memorandum of understanding between the main commercial parties envisage work beginning on the long-delayed project within the next three months.
Target date for completion is before year 2000.

The 41-level tower building would be built at a cost of A$251 million on an 8,000 square metre site left by demolition of the old Waltons retail building in 1987 after its purchase by the failed Bond Corp group.
Citibank Ltd, the Australian arm of U.S.-based Citicorp Ltd, was expected to join the development consortium but was waiting on development go-ahead, the Caburah spokesman said.
